description: The vanilla Skyrim FARMHOUSE INTERIOR tileset, packaged as the linked inside for every farmhouse-shell exterior (interiors_index TILESET_RULES already names this kit for `vanilla:architecture/farmhouse/`; owner rule 2026-09-05: a building with an interior must have a door that teleports to a LINKED interior kit, so the kit has to exist as built and measured geometry). Pure packaging of `meshes/architecture/farmhouse/interior/`: the `farmint` family that Bethesda uses inside every Skyrim farmhouse, inn and longhouse, plus the `farmb` basement family below it and the two farmhouse load doors that are the link itself. Three room grammars ship in one directory and are kept apart in snapLogic: the plain `farmint` cottage shell, the `farmint2` second cottage shell, and the `farmintlh` longhouse with its loft. Chosen over any mod source because these ARE the meshes against which the exterior shells in TILESET_RULES were authored: the interior walls line up with the outside walls of `farmhouse01-06`, `inn01` and `farmlonghouse01`, which no substitute set can claim.

snapLogic.cottage-farmint: The base cottage shell. `farmintend01/02/03` are the three gable-end shells; `farmintwall01` is the straight bay that extends the room between ends; `farmintcorner01` turns it; `farmintdoorway01` is the wall bay carrying an interior doorway; `farmintwallhearth01/02` replace a wall bay with the hearth. `farmintwooddoorway01`, `farmintwoodend01/02` and `farmintwoodwall01` are the timber-partition variants of the same bays and substitute one-for-one. `farmintwbasementent01` is the wall bay that opens the stair down to the basement family. Bays butt face-to-face on a 3.6 m (256-unit) module with the origin on the floor plane at the bay centre; a small room is two ends back to back, a medium room ends plus two walls, a large room ends plus four walls and a corner.
snapLogic.cottage-farmint2: The second cottage shell — a DIFFERENT authored grid, not a variant set. `farmint2end01/02/03` its ends, `farmint2wall01` its bay, `farmint2doorway03/04` its doorways (`farmint2doorway02nodoor` is the same opening with no door leaf), `farmint2hearth02` its hearth and `farmint2basementent01` its basement stair. Do not interleave `farmint` and `farmint2` bays in one room; change set at a doorway.
snapLogic.inn: `farmintinnend01-06` are the inn's six end/corner shells with `farmintinnwall01` between them and `farmintinnwallentrance01` at the entry. Same 256-unit module as the cottage but taller, so it makes the two-storey common room; it is the large-room option.
snapLogic.longhouse: `farmintlhbase01/02` are the floor plates, `farmintlhfront01` and `farmintlhback01` the two ends, `farmintlhmid01` the extension bay, `farmintlhend01/02` the closing walls, `farmintlhfirepit01-03` the central fire, and `farmintlhloft01/02` + `farmintlhlofttop01` the loft deck over the aisle. Stack loft pieces on the base plates, never on the cottage grid.
snapLogic.basement: `farmb*` is the cellar below any of the above and has its own grid: `farmbmiddle01/02` floor bays, `farmbwall01-04` walls, `farmbcorner01-04` outside and `farmbicorner01-04` inside corners, `farmbdivider01-04` the internal partitions, `farmbcolumn01/02` the props, `farmbwallentrance01-05` the wall bays that receive the stair up, and `farmbtrapdoor01/02` + `farmbwalltrapdoor01` the trapdoor way up. `farmbwell01`/`farmbwellent01` are the well shaft. `farmhousejaildoor01` is the barred door for a cellar lock-up.
snapLogic.load-doors: `farmhousedoor01` and `farmhouseldoor01` are the exterior leaves the teleport link uses — placed in the exterior shell's doorway opening, they are the visible half of the door that carries the player into this kit.
snapLogic.unitScale: Bethesda units; 0.0142240 m/unit. Measured extents per piece in tooling/asset-pipeline/output/kits/vanilla-farmhouse-int.kit.json.
